_comment: Pinned query covers for gallery/neighbors.html. Not sampled per run: the
same twelve covers every time, so two reviewers looking at the panel on
different days are looking at the same thing.
Selection, by group:
famous      recognisable covers, so a reviewer can judge neighbour quality
against their own knowledge of the record.
v2-3-hard   covers the v2-3 palette algorithm demonstrably failed on. These
were matched into music-artworks by CONTENT (sha256 of the file
bytes), not by filename -- the eval keeps them in images/ under
short names, and 7 of the 25 turn out to be byte-identical to a
file already in the corpus.
v2-3-hard-proxy
working-set stand-ins for three v2-3-hard covers that turned out
to be HELD OUT. They are not themselves v2-3 failures and must
never be described as such -- they are the nearest working-set
artworks to the covers they replace.
HELD-OUT QUERY REPLACEMENT (2026-08-03, closes review finding C-new-2):
Three of the original twelve -- 'johns', 'krafty' and 'muse' -- were in the
frozen holdout (data/holdout/holdout.json), so rendering this panel put three
held-out artworks in front of a reviewer. gallery.py already calls a held-out
query 'an editing mistake, not a sampling accident'; this is the edit.
Selection rule, applied mechanically and stated so it can be re-run:
1. Rank all other corpus artworks by cosine to the removed cover under the
CANONICAL embedding -- dinov2-vitl14 at native 224 px, per decision
d-2026-08-02-embedding-canonical-model. Vectors are L2-normalized
(verified: norms within 1.2e-7 of 1.0), so cosine is a plain dot product.
2. Keep the highest-ranked artwork that is in the WORKING SET -- open under
holdout.json, i.e. neither held nor quarantined -- and not already pinned.
3. CROSS-ARM SAME-FAMILY SCREEN: reject any candidate whose maximum cosine to
any rendition of the removed cover, over all six embedding arms, is >= 0.80.
This step is load-bearing, not decoration. For 'muse' the mechanical winner
of steps 1-2 was b9202199ce8e738fce42630101615c28, which is Muse 'Showbiz' --
the same record family under a different artwork id. The canonical arm reads
it at only 0.68, below the 0.95 census threshold, so the near-duplicate
census never flagged it and the holdout's zero-crossing-edges guarantee is
untouched. But pe-core-l14 reads it at 0.906 and siglip2-so400m at 0.916 --
and pe-core is the arm GALLERY_NOTES.md eliminated precisely BECAUSE it
matches by artist. Pinning it would have put a near-relative of a held-out
cover back on the page under a different filename. The three covers actually
chosen top out at 0.587 / 0.608 / 0.528 across all six arms, so the screen
separates cleanly and is not a tuned threshold.
Verified after the edit: all twelve pinned covers now classify as 'open'.
The removed covers stay in the record. GALLERY_NOTES.md observations that name
johns, krafty or muse are HISTORICAL RECORD of what a reviewer actually saw on
the browse of 2026-08-02, and are deliberately left untouched -- that file is
sha-pinned evidence. Nothing here retroactively edits what was observed; it only
changes what the panel renders from now on.
distinctive covers with the LOWEST best-neighbour cosine across all three
finalists, i.e. the corpus's genuine visual outliers, chosen by
measurement rather than by browsing.
random-300  seeded draw from the 300 px tier, to show what the models do
with a low-detail thumbnail.
loups.jpg and doja.jpg were requested but are NOT present in either corpus by
content hash, so they cannot be shown without embedding them ad hoc.

queries.label: System of a Down — Toxicity
queries.why: Globally recognisable. Photographic scene, heavy grain, hillside lettering integrated into the artwork plus a separate red title overlay — two different kinds of text in one cover.

queries.label: Green Day — American Idiot
queries.why: Globally recognisable, and does triple duty: flat black field with white/red vector art, a parental-advisory badge in the corner, and a known v2-3 failure (the algorithm reversed the black background and white foreground).

queries.label: flood, wave and grandfather clock (stand-in for v2-3 'johns')
queries.replaces: music-artworks/8/7/e/87e9beeb1ba665f10b446ae57c79b672.jpg — The Longest Johns, Between Wind and Water; removed 2026-08-03 as held-out
queries.why: Nearest working-set artwork to the held-out 'johns' cover under the canonical arm (0.4846; rank 3 overall, the two above it are both held out). Stands in for the same property: a large blue-green water field filling the lower two thirds, which is exactly what the v2-3 ask 'we are really missing the sailor blue surface' was about. Flat-colour comic illustration — a Hokusai-style breaking wave, a slumped figure at a flooded table, a drowning grandfather clock and TV, a big orange moon on a pink/mauve sky. Note it is NOT a v2-3 failure case; no v2-3 verdict exists for it.

queries.label: Valeria — #100tete mas Barranquillero (stand-in for v2-3 'krafty')
queries.why: Nearest working-set artwork to the held-out 'krafty' cover under the canonical arm (0.5644; the three above it are all held out). Carries krafty's diagnostic property — the wanted colour lives in the LETTERING, not in area. Dense tropical floral border (magenta, red, yellow, green) around a near-black centre, with large white brush script, a yellow crown and multi-coloured hand-lettered type. If a model returns neighbours that match the black field rather than the type, that is the same failure krafty exposed. NOT itself a v2-3 failure case.

queries.label: American Horror Story: Apocalypse — The Supreme Playlist (stand-in for v2-3 'muse')
queries.why: Highest-ranked working-set artwork to the held-out 'muse' cover that survives the cross-arm same-family screen (0.4312 on the canonical arm; the mechanical winner above it was a different pressing of the same record and was rejected — see the selection rule in _comment). Carries muse's diagnostic property: dark-on-dark with one hot accent, the case where midpoint and background both collapse to near-black. Silhouetted figure before an orange/amber fire on a near-black ground, chrome title, and a long block of yellow-outlined tracklist text. NOT itself a v2-3 failure case.

queries.label: v2-3 'infected'
queries.why: The ask that is provably unreachable: the reviewer wanted a blue that 'no measurable property' separates from the rest. If any model puts visually blue covers next to this one, that is a hint the property exists in embedding space even though it did not exist in colorimetry.

queries.label: fly agaric on forest floor
queries.why: The single most isolated cover in the corpus — lowest best-neighbour cosine averaged across all three finalists (dinov2 0.180 / pe-core 0.468 / dinov3 0.170). One sharp red subject on dark bokeh: exactly the has_dominant_subject + has_accent_color case the palette cares about.

queries.label: boarding passes on black
queries.why: PE-Core put this cover in a cluster of its OWN (size 1) — the only degenerate cluster in any of the three models. All three agree it is an outlier (best neighbour 0.39-0.48). Red and white paper documents, dense fine print, pure black ground.

queries.label: Monĕsk — Departure
queries.why: Near-monochrome fog photograph, very low chroma, thin grey type. The 'has_accent_color = false' case — if a model returns colourful neighbours here it is not reading chroma at all.

queries.label: baroque pavilion, muted photograph
queries.why: Highly isolated (dinov2 0.152, the lowest single score in the sample) and a 300 px thumbnail, so it tests outlier behaviour and low resolution at the same time. Desaturated architectural photograph with no text at all.

queries.label: random 300 px thumbnail (1 of 2)
queries.why: Seeded draw from the 2,917-file 300 px tier. Included unfiltered: a sanity check should contain some covers nobody chose for being interesting.

queries.label: random 300 px thumbnail (2 of 2)
queries.why: Seeded draw from the 300 px tier. At this resolution small text and label logos are physically illegible, so neighbours driven by fine detail are suspect.
